question: In a race, an athlete covers a distance of 300 m in 100 sec in the first lap. He covers the second lap of the same length in 50 sec. What is the average speed (in m/sec) of the athlete?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 300 + 300 = 600 m

Total time = 100 + 50 = 150 sec

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

= 600 ÷ 150 = 4 m/sec

**∴ Answer = 4 m/sec**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of each lap = 300 m

Time taken = 100 sec and 50 sec

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 300 + 300 = 600 m

⇒ Total time = 100 + 50 = 150 sec

⇒ Average speed = 600 ÷ 150 = 4 m/sec

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m/sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Total distance ÷ total time

Important Note

Do not average speeds directly

Key Insight

Use combined distance and time
